1: Verily, all this is Brahman. From him do all things originate, into him do they dissolve, through him do they live. Him alone should one worship in silence.
Man is made of will (kratu). According as his will is in this world, so will he be when he has departed this life. Let him therefore form this will:
Man is made of mind. According as his thought is in this world, so will he be when he has departed this life. Let him therefore form this thought.
2: [Chandogya 6.8.7 — Tat tvam asi: That thou art]
Bring hither a fruit of that nyagrodha (banyan) tree.

Here it is, venerable sir. Break it. It is broken, venerable sir. What do you see there? These seeds, almost infinitesimal. Break one of them. It is broken, venerable sir. What do you see there? Nothing at all, venerable sir.
Then he said to him: My son, that subtle essence which you do not perceive there, of that very essence this great nyagrodha tree exists.
Believe it, my son. That which is that subtle essence, in it all that exists has its self. It is the True. It is the Self, and thou, O Svetaketu, art it.
